old.name: Gundulićeva Poljana — Old Town morning market
old.text: The Old Town morning market under Gundulić's statue (Frangeš-Mihanović 1893). Closes early — by 14:00 the stalls fold. Best for: candied bitter-orange peel (arancini, the Dubrovnik confection), lavender from Hvar, dried figs, herb bunches, and the cold-pressed olive oils in glass bottles. Smaller than Gruž, more touristed; less for fish, better for confections to take back to the boat. Address Gundulić Square, Old Town

old.name: Mali Ston quay (oysters direct)
old.text: Not a market in the formal sense — but the oyster boats from the bay tie up at the Mali Ston quay through the season and sell oysters and mussels directly. Bring a clean basket, ice, and small bills. The Bota Šare farm has a fixed dock stall most mornings; ask at the restaurant if no one is at the quay. PDO 2020/1469 Ostrea edulis at zero kilometres. Address Mali Ston waterfront, Pelješac

old.name: Saints Hills — Oskorušno, Pelješac + Komarna
old.text: The Tolj family estate with the Rolland consulting badge. Flagships: Sv. Lucija Dingač and Sv. Roko Komarna. Also Istrian whites (Mala Nevina). Open tasting room with food pairing; one of the easier Pelješac visits to book.

old.name: Uje — Croatian olive oils
old.text: The Uje brand selects from Croatian estates — Istrian and Dalmatian. The Konavle oils (smaller estates than the famous Istrian ones, but very respectable) and the Korčula oils are the ones to bring back. Salt-flake selections from the Ston pans; rakija pours by the small bottle. Tasting flights at the back. Address Placa 5, Old Town

provisioning:Uje.brief: Verify Uje trades in 2026 at Placa (Stradun); the old card says 'Placa 5'.

old.name: Franciscan Monastery Pharmacy (1317)
old.text: Founded 1317; the third-oldest pharmacy in the world counting non-continuous operations, and the oldest still-operating one in Europe . Sells rose creams, sage soaps, almond oils and pine balms made from the friars' historical recipes. The shop is at the front of the Monastery; the museum-pharmacy hall behind (EUR 6 entry) preserves the 14th-c. apothecary. Address Stradun 2, Old Town

old.name: Asia Shop Dubrovnik
old.label: ASIAN
old.text: The serviceable Asian grocer of the city — soy, mirin, gochujang, sushi rice, nori, rice vinegars, Thai curries, kecap manis. Stock changes; call ahead for specific items. The one address a charter kitchen needs for a Japanese guest request. Where Lapad · Iva Vojnovića 32

old.name: Konzum on Gundulićeva Poljana
old.label: SUPERMARKET
old.text: The supermarket Old-Town locals actually use — sane prices on bottled water (3–5× cheaper than Stradun café markups), Croatian basics, the Dolcela baking shelf, and the reliable Vegeta-and-Podravka aisle for Balkan pantry classics. Where Pile · just outside the gate

old.name: City Walls loop
old.text: The full ring: Pile entry → up the Bokar bastion → south wall sea-side → Minčeta (25 m, highest point) → back down to Pile. Stone reads 38–42 °C in full sun; no shade on the second half. EUR 35 combined ticket with Lovrijenac, EUR 25 walls only. Buy at the Pile booth or online to skip the first 20 min.

old_also.name: City Walls — Minčeta, Bokar, Lovrijenac
old_also.label: 1,940 m · 13TH–17TH C
chips: Early or late — never midday in summer
old_also.text: Best walked 07:30 or 17:30 · ~1.5 h loop EUR 35 (combined Walls + Lovrijenac) BOOK-AHEAD Early or late — never midday in summer The walls run 1,940 metres around the Old Town. Maximum height 25 m at the Minčeta Tower (1464, circular Renaissance fort by Michelozzo and Juraj Dalmatinac, with 6 m-thick cannon-deflecting walls). Bokar (1461–63, Michelozzo two-storey casemate) juts forward to flank the Pile Gate. Lovrijenac (St Lawrence) — "Dubrovnik's Gibraltar" — stands on a detached 37 m rock outside the western walls, with seaward walls 12 m thick and city-facing walls only 60 cm so the city could collapse it from within if captured. The inscription over its door: Non bene pro toto libertas venditur auro . Walk the loop at 07:30 or between 17:30 and 18:30 — the stone reads 38–42 °C in full sun and there is no shade on the second half. Where Old Town · ring road on stone

old.name: Stradun five-squares walk
old.text: Pile (Onofrio's fountain, 1438) → small Onofrio's fountain in Luža Square (Sponza + St Blaise's Church + Bell Tower + Orlando's Column 1418) → Gundulić Square (morning market, statue of Ivan Gundulić by Frangeš-Mihanović 1893) → Poljana Boškovića (Jesuit Stairs + St Ignatius) → Bunić (the Old Port view, with Lokrum on the horizon). Walk it before 09:00. The Stradun limestone is polished perilously slick in rain.

old.name: Mount Srđ cable car + Fort Imperial
old.text: The cable car climbs from above Buža 412 m to the summit of Srđ (3 min). Fort Imperial (Napoleon 1812) houses the Museum of Croatian War of Independence — the city's siege story, told from the mountain that the defenders held. Restaurant Panorama for a sunset drink. EUR 27 return .

old.name: Ston walls walk + salt pans
old.text: Begun 1333 when Ston joined the Republic. 5.5 km — the longest stone defensive walls in Europe still standing. The walk climbs sharply over the Stonsko polje saddle to Mali Ston on the bay side. The Ston salt pans below (still in production after 4,000 years; harvest by hand July–September) supplied the Republic's salt monopoly. Combine with oyster lunch at Bota Šare.

old.name: Konavle Ljuta river + watermills walk
old.text: Drive 35 min south to the Ljuta river in Konavle. Walk upstream from Konavoski Dvori through the watermills (some still grind in autumn). The river is cold-spring fed; air drops 5 °C beside the channel. Lunch at Konoba Konavoski Dvori — frog brodet, trout, lamb peka.
